subject: general
question: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the founder of the **Maurya Empire**, which was established in 321 BCE in ancient India.
 
• He unified most of the Indian subcontinent under one empire, laying the foundation for centralized governance.
 
• With the guidance of his advisor and mentor **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, Chandragupta implemented administrative and economic reforms.
 
• The Maurya Empire under Chandragupta’s rule extended across northern India and parts of present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• He is also known for defeating the Nanda dynasty and repelling the invasion attempts of Seleucus I Nicator, a general of Alexander the Great.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chanakya (Kautilya):**

 
 
• Chanakya was a key advisor and strategist for Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• He authored the **Arthashastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on politics, economics, and statecraft.
 
• Chanakya played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Maurya Empire by mentoring Chandragupta and devising military and political strategies.
 
 
 
• **The Maurya Empire:**
 
 
• The Maurya Empire (321 BCE–185 BCE) was one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• It was marked by centralized governance, a strong military, and advancements in trade, economics, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Seleucus I Nicator:**
 
 
• He was a general of Alexander the Great who attempted to reclaim Indian territories after Alexander’s death.
 
• Chandragupta defeated Seleucus I and secured a peace treaty that included a matrimonial alliance.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Chandragupta Maurya:**
 
 
• Chandragupta’s establishment of the Maurya Empire marked the beginning of large-scale political unity in India.
 
• He is regarded as one of the most significant rulers in Indian history for his role in unifying the subcontinent.
